story.title: Jensen Huang went to war with Washington — and won a path to China - The Washington Post

facts.text: Huang, the leather-jacket-clad CEO of the world's most important chipmaker, resigned from Nvidia on Thursday after revelations that he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy .

But the spy saga is gripping Washington, and lawmakers are preparing for investigations into how the now-ex-CEO's affair may have damaged U.S. artificial intelligence dominance, the national security implications and the executive's close relationship with President Donald Trump and his Cabinet.
The calls for immediate investigation into Huang and Nvidia on the day of his resignation represent a stunning fall from grace in the halls of power for the former CEO.
Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer , D-N.Y., in a post to X on Thursday, said "Congress must demand answers from Mr.

Huang and the woman with whom he reportedly had a relationship, Alice Huang, an executive at the Singaporean technology company Megaspeed and an alleged Chinese spy have drawn congressional attention.

The New York Times reported on Monday that Nvidia's general counsel, Tim Teter, claimed in emails to Commerce investigators probing Alice Huang's company that he'd been in touch with Jeffrey Kessler, who leads BIS.
The Commerce investigation into Megaspeed, which allegedly smuggled restricted chips to China, was then transferred to the Justice Department.
Elizabeth Warren , D-Mass., the likely incoming chair of the Senate banking panel, said in a statement Thursday that "Mr.
Huang, NVIDIA executives, and NVIDIA's board of directors still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls
"He is always the TED Talk guy," one senior Democratic staff member who was granted anonymity to describe private meetings they had attended with Huang, told CNBC.
"He's really good and articulate, and really good at explaining why AI is important and why it's so important for the United States to be leading here."
The senators who will lead those investigations, and hold subpoena power in the new Congress, are gearing up for Nvidia to take center stage.

House Foreign Affairs Committee Chair Brian Mast , R-Fla., is actively negotiating for Huang to testify before House committees and told reporters Thursday the Nvidia CEO has agreed to appear in the coming weeks.
For years, Nvidia founder Jensen Huang and his lobbyists barreled through Washington seeking to secure the company’s right to sell its powerful artificial intelligence chips to China.

The Washington Post on November 23, 2026 reported that Jensen Huang and Nvidia’s Washington operation spent years fighting to keep selling advanced AI chips in China — including direct calls from Huang that two people familiar with the effort described as part of a campaign that was “constantly and aggressively” lobbying.
Ian Duncan’s story frames a trail of mistrust in the capital even as Commerce has already approved hundreds of thousands of China-bound licenses.
For builders, the point is not gossip about meetings: policy access and license rows are different levers , and only one of them shows up in your export-compliance checklist.
Because the November 23 Post excerpt is short, CNBC’s November 9, 2026 feature remains the richest on-the-record stack on Huang’s White House relationship and federal lobbying dollars .
CNBC writes that Huang spent roughly two years building “unparalleled” access to President Donald Trump , influencing federal AI policy while pushing looser China restrictions .
Treat video titles as editorial framing , not statutes.

Readers searching “did lobbying win China access?” should read CNBC’s last bullet: Washington approvals did not automatically clear Chinese customs .

McGuire’s public commentary after the Megaspeed reporting — including a November 2026 thread on X reproduced in CNBC’s follow-up — argued that Commerce should tighten export controls so firms linked to intelligence risks cannot keep buying frontier GPUs .
